actions.text: My notes say the carry shortcut in the scalar Montgomery reduction is real but only reaches about 0.9933. The borrow-chain n2/n3 rewrite and the all-ones shift tricks are dead ends. This time I'll keep the carry shortcut and pair it with a second saving in the same mul/reduce path.

actions.diff:
--- a/secp256r1/src/scalar.rs
+++ b/secp256r1/src/scalar.rs
@@ -556,3 +556,11 @@
-    reduce_wide([r4, r5, r6, r7, r8])
-}
-
+    reduce_wide([r4, r5, r6, r7, r8])
+}
+
+/// Returns the carry out of `r + k * MODULUS[0]`, whose low word is zero by
+/// the choice of `k`: the low product word is `0` when `r == 0` and `2^64 - r`
+/// otherwise.
+#[inline(always)]
+fn low_word_carry(r: u64, k: u64) -> u64 {
+    (((k as u128) * (MODULUS[0] as u128)) >> 64) as u64 + u64::from(r != 0)
+}
+

actions.reason:
Changes to secp256r1/src/scalar.rs, all producing identical values:
1. montgomery_reduce_words: the low word of r_i + k*n0 is zero by construction of k, so the carry out of that word is hi(k*n0) + (r_i != 0). The full mac on n0 in each of the four rounds is replaced by a high-product computation (low_word_carry).
2. reduce_wide and reduce_sum return early when there is no top carry and the fourth limb is below MODULUS[3]. That condition implies value < n, so the complement-add chain is skipped in the common case.
3. Sub computes the +n correction only when the subtraction borrowed.
Measured scalar_arith_ir ratio 0.9741, field_arith_ir 0.9999, outputs identical in the equivalence harness.

journal.text:
Worked on secp256r1/src/scalar.rs to cut instruction count on scalar_arith_ir. In montgomery_reduce_words the low word of r_i + k*n0 is zero by construction of k, so its carry out is hi(k*n0) + (r_i != 0). I replaced the full mac on n0 in each of the four rounds with a high-product helper, low_word_carry. I also added early returns in reduce_wide and reduce_sum for the no-top-carry case.

Evaluation 1 was rejected: ratio 0.9940 against a required 0.9900. Evaluation 3 was rejected at 0.9906. Evaluation 5 was accepted: scalar_arith_ir went from 363385810 to 353957627, ratio 0.9741. field_arith_ir was 0.9999. All three had identical outputs. Submitted at 34 changed lines; replay verdict pending.

The reduction loop carries real redundant work. The partial edits on their own were not enough; the combination is what crossed the line.

Next: look at the square path and invert for the same zero-low-word carry pattern. field.rs may have the same reduce structure.
